newsitem.title: POLAND: ZASADA TO ISSUE CONVERTIBLE BONDS.
newsitem.headline: ZASADA TO ISSUE CONVERTIBLE BONDS.

text.p: Polish automotive group Sobieslaw Zasada Centrum SA plans to issue convertible bonds to increase its investment and change the company's financing structure, the company's spokesman said on Friday.

"We are planning to issue convertible bonds. The size of the issue has not been decided yet... The issue is, first of all, linked with our future investment and the change in the company's finacing structure," Marcin Trzaska told Reuters.
Trzaska added the decision on the bond issue would be taken at the shareholders meeting on August 28.

Parkiet, the Polish bourse paper, said on Friday that the bond issue would amount to 90 million zlotys but Trzaska said that even though this figure had been considered it could still change radically.
"It is nothing certain yet and the figure can radically change, it can rather go up," Trzaska said.
He said the bonds would be convertible to between 500,000 and five million shares of series C, the issue of which was planned in 1996 but not carried out.
Trzaska said the bond issue would be mainly offered to large investors.
